Thanks for the clear context, Alicia — this is exactly the right set of questions before committing. Short answer up front: mixed is often the best cost/latency tradeoff for dual workloads, but there are situations where H100-only simplifies SLOs and reduces operational complexity. Below are practical tradeoffs and a ballpark proposal; attaching a short pricing PDF.

High-level guidance:
- H100-only (80GB): Best per-token latency for chat (esp. long contexts, quantized tokens), higher price per GPU-hour but often wins on latency-critical workloads. Easier to guarantee low-latency SLOs.
- A100(40GB): Good for dense batching (embeddings) with strong perf/$ on high-throughput embedding pipelines. Less headroom for large chat contexts.
- L40S(48GB): Lowest cost of the three for many inference stacks, competitive for embeddings and medium-length chat if you can accept slightly higher tail latency.

Commit structuring (ballpark):
- 12-month reserved commit with 20% minimum utilization target: typical discounts in our quote tiers are 18–30% vs on-demand depending on mix and minimum commit.
- Mixed fleet recommendation for Optimo: keep ~40% H100 capacity (chat), 60% A100/L40S (embeddings) — this preserves SLOs for chat while minimizing cost for bulk embeddings.

I've attached 'redwood-dedicated-pricing-v3.pdf' with three illustrative tiers and a sample canary rollout plan. Neha and Priyom — please add specifics on throughput guarantees and pool sizing assumptions below (cc'd).

Next step: if you can drop your weekly token forecast (or the spreadsheet), I can run a quick sizing model and send a recommended commit with expected monthly $ and perf/$ numbers. Happy to do a 30-min call if you prefer.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — technical perf/$ estimates and pool-sizing notes

Markus / Alicia — adding technical estimates to make the tradeoffs concrete. Assumptions: chat 350 tokens avg, seq len tail to ~1k tokens occasionally; embeddings batch sizes variable, we assume ~3M vectors/day distributed across off-peak. We assume FP16/AMP inference with int8 where validated.

Rough sustained throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU (real workloads, typical model family):
- H100 (80GB): ~18k tokens/sec (generative chat), excellent headroom for long context; memory allows larger KV cache + bigger models.
- A100 (40GB): ~9–11k tokens/sec (chat) when quantized to FP16; best when used for batched embeddings where throughput per dollar is high.
- L40S (48GB): ~8–10k tokens/sec (chat), comparable to A100 on many runs but lower peak for very long contexts; excels on embeddings perf/$ when using batched execution paths.

Embeddings throughput (vectors/sec) per GPU (batched):
- A100: ~450–600 vectors/sec (large-batch optimized kernels) depending on batch size and model topology.
- L40S: ~420–580 vectors/sec, slightly cheaper per hour.
- H100: ~500–700 vectors/sec but higher hourly cost — useful when embeddings and chat share hot KV cache or model variants.

Performance per dollar considerations (very approximate):
- If your workload is 70% embeddings / 30% chat, A100 or L40S-heavy pool typically gives best $/month for same throughput.
- If chat is >50% or requires <150ms tail latency, H100 share should increase for SLO headroom.

Autoscaling & burst behavior with mixed fleets:
- Autoscale is per GPU-pool. Mixed fleet managed by policy: traffic routed to preferred GPU type first (H100), then overflow to compatible A100/L40S variants with degraded latency estimates.
- Commit-level throughput guarantees: we can guarantee pooled throughput at the commit level for equivalent model variants, but must define acceptable latency degradation tiers for overflow. For strict SLOs, you can reserve a minimum committed H100 slice and use mixed fleet only for best-effort capacity.

Alicia — great questions. Short answers and a concrete next step below.

1) Throughput SLA: we can guarantee committed pooled throughput for a named model family and EMU (model variant) provided you reserve a minimum H100 slice for latency-critical traffic. That SLA will specify tokens/sec and a 95th/99th latency threshold; overflow to A100/L40S is explicitly marked as "best-effort" in the SLA unless you accept larger commit tiers that include burst H100 capacity. We'll include explicit audit logging for fallbacks.

2) Discounts & credits: our standard public tiers: 12-mo reserved: 18–24% discount; 24-mo reserved: 24–30% discount (depends on GPU mix and utilization commitment). For early customers we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to ~1 month of committed spend and a 30-day free canary window for the H100 minimum slice (requires signed contract).

3) Model pinning & rollouts: Redwood Console supports per-route pinning (route->model->gpu-variant). Rollouts can be canaried by traffic %, region, or commit-tier. Fallbacks are logged and surfaced in the Console audit trail; we'll include the standard wording in the addendum.

- I will run a sizing model against the spreadsheet you uploaded and return a recommended commit mix with monthly $ and perf/$ at three discount tiers by EOD Friday.
